string-array.name: facts_animals
string-array.item: A blue whale\'s heart is as big as a small car, and it can be heard from over a mile away!
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
A group of flamingos is called a \"flamboyance.\"
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they don\'t drift apart.
A snail can sleep for three years straight!
Elephants are the only animals that can\'t jump.
A hummingbird\'s heart beats over 1,200 times per minute.
Cows have best friends and get stressed when separated from them.
A single giant tortoise can live for more than 150 years.
Koalas have fingerprints so similar to humans that they could confuse a crime scene!
Butterflies taste with their feet.
A shrimp\'s heart is located in its head.
Polar bears have black skin under their white fur to help absorb heat.
A woodpecker can peck a tree up to 20 times per second.
Kangaroos can\'t walk backwards.
The tongue of a giraffe can be up to 20 inches (50 cm) long.
Starfish don\'t have brains or blood.
An ostrich\'s eye is bigger than its brain.
Dolphins give each other names — special clicks just for one dolphin friend.
A cheetah can go from 0 to 60 mph in about 3 seconds.
Some frogs can freeze solid in winter and thaw out alive in spring.
A crocodile cannot stick its tongue out.
Honeybees can recognize human faces.
A group of crows is called a \"murder.\"
The blue whale is the loudest animal on Earth — louder than a jet engine!
Some ants can carry objects 50 times their own body weight.
A group of pandas is called an \"embarrassment.\"
Sloths only poop about once a week.
An electric eel can produce a shock strong enough to stun a horse.
Penguins propose to their mates with a pebble.

string-array.name: facts_space
string-array.item: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus!
The footprints left by astronauts on the Moon will stay there for millions of years — there\'s no wind to blow them away.
One million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
Saturn could float in water because it\'s mostly made of gas.
A neutron star is so dense that a teaspoon of it would weigh billions of tons.
There are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on every beach on Earth.
Space is completely silent because there\'s no air to carry sound.
Jupiter has the shortest day of all the planets — it spins all the way around in about 10 hours.
The largest known star, UY Scuti, is so big that Earth would look like a tiny dot next to it.
On Mars, the sunsets look blue instead of orange.
An entire year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.
Astronauts grow up to 2 inches (5 cm) taller in space because their spine stretches out.
There is a giant storm on Jupiter, called the Great Red Spot, that has been raging for hundreds of years.
The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth — about 1.5 inches (3.8 cm) every year.
It would take more than a thousand years to walk to the Moon.
The International Space Station travels around the Earth 16 times every single day.
Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
A cloud of gas in space, called a nebula, can be trillions of miles wide.
If you could drive a car to the Sun, it would take over 176 years.
Saturn\'s rings are made mostly of ice and rock, and some pieces are as small as a grain of sugar.
The Sun makes up about 99.8% of all the mass in our entire solar system.
There is a planet made almost entirely of diamond, discovered by scientists in 2004.
Mercury has no atmosphere, so its temperature can swing from freezing to scorching in the same day.
Black holes don\'t actually \"suck\" things in — objects fall toward them because of gravity, just like on Earth.
A full spacesuit costs more than $12 million.
The Milky Way galaxy is on a slow collision course with a neighboring galaxy, but it won\'t happen for billions of years.
You can\'t hear yourself burp in space, because sound needs air to travel.
Uranus rotates on its side, so it basically rolls around the Sun like a ball.
The footprints on the Moon are from Apollo astronauts, but only 12 people have ever walked there.
Comets are sometimes called \"dirty snowballs\" because they\'re made of ice, dust, and rock.

string-array.name: facts_dinosaurs
string-array.item: Some dinosaurs, like Velociraptor, were actually about the size of a turkey — not giant like in movies!
The word \"dinosaur\" means \"terrible lizard\" in Greek.
The Argentinosaurus may have weighed as much as 10 elephants.
Some dinosaurs had feathers, just like birds today.
Birds are actually the closest living relatives of dinosaurs.
The Tyrannosaurus rex had teeth as long as bananas.
A Stegosaurus\'s brain was about the size of a walnut.
The largest dinosaur eggs ever found were about the size of a basketball.
Some dinosaurs, like the Spinosaurus, could swim and hunt fish in rivers.
Triceratops had one of the largest skulls of any land animal ever, up to 8 feet (2.4 m) long.
Dinosaurs lived on Earth for over 165 million years before disappearing.
Not all giant prehistoric creatures were dinosaurs — flying pterosaurs and swimming plesiosaurs were different animal groups.
Some small dinosaurs were about the size of a chicken.
Scientists believe some dinosaurs could run as fast as 30 miles per hour.
The very first dinosaur fossil was officially named in 1824.
A group of Deinonychus may have hunted together in packs, much like wolves.
Some long-necked dinosaurs, like Brachiosaurus, could reach leaves 30 feet (9 m) up in trees.
Fossilized dinosaur footprints can show scientists how fast a dinosaur was walking or running.
The Microraptor was a dinosaur small enough to fit in your hand and may have been able to glide.
Many dinosaurs laid eggs in nests, just like birds do today.
Scientists can sometimes tell what a dinosaur ate by studying fossilized poop, called coprolites!
The Ankylosaurus had a giant bony club at the end of its tail for defense.
Pterosaurs, flying reptiles from the dinosaur age, had wingspans as wide as a small airplane.
Some dinosaur fossils have been found with preserved skin, showing bumpy, scaly textures.
The Compsognathus was one of the smallest known dinosaurs, about the size of a cat.
Many plant-eating dinosaurs had teeth built specifically for grinding tough leaves.
Scientists think some dinosaurs may have been warm-blooded, more like birds than lizards.
The longest dinosaur trackway ever found stretches for miles across ancient mud that turned to stone.
A Parasaurolophus had a long, curved crest on its head that may have made loud trumpeting sounds.
Most of what we know about dinosaurs comes from studying fossilized bones buried for millions of years.

string-array.name: facts_nature_records
string-array.item: The tallest tree in the world, a redwood named Hyperion, is taller than a 30-story building.
Antarctica is technically the world\'s largest desert because it gets so little precipitation.
The Amazon Rainforest produces about 20% of the world\'s oxygen.
Mount Everest grows about 4 millimeters taller every year.
The Sahara Desert is almost as big as the entire United States.
Lightning can be five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The deepest part of the ocean, the Mariana Trench, is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.
A single bolt of lightning contains enough energy to toast about 100,000 slices of bread.
The largest living organism on Earth is a fungus in Oregon that covers almost 4 square miles.
The Dead Sea is so salty that people can float on top of it without even trying.
The fastest wind speed ever recorded on Earth was over 250 miles per hour, during a tornado.
Niagara Falls moves so much water that it could fill an Olympic swimming pool in about one second.
The world\'s largest snowflake on record was reportedly 15 inches wide.
Death Valley is the hottest place in North America, with ground temperatures over 200°F (93°C).
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, visible even from space.
A single raindrop falls at about 20 miles per hour.
The largest desert flower, the corpse flower, can smell like rotting meat to attract insects.
Some parts of Chile\'s Atacama Desert have never recorded a single drop of rain.
The tallest waterfall in the world, Angel Falls, drops for almost 3,200 feet.
The largest cave chamber in the world could fit multiple jumbo jets inside it.
Glaciers hold about 70% of all the fresh water on Earth.
A rainbow is actually a full circle, but we usually only see half of it from the ground.
The coldest temperature ever recorded on Earth was about -128°F (-89°C) in Antarctica.
The Amazon River carries more water than the next seven biggest rivers combined.
Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants and can grow almost 3 feet (91 cm) in a single day.
The largest volcano in our solar system is actually on Mars, not Earth.
Some redwood trees alive today were already growing before ancient Rome existed.
The Sahara Desert was once green and covered in lakes, thousands of years ago.
The world\'s largest hailstone was almost as big as a volleyball.
Iceberg tips are just the top — about 90% of an iceberg hides underwater.

string-array.name: facts_math
string-array.item: Zero is the only number that can\'t be represented in Roman numerals.
A \"googol\" is the number 1 followed by 100 zeros — way bigger than the company Google\'s name comes from!
The symbol for infinity (∞) is called a \"lemniscate.\"
If you add up all the numbers from 1 to 100, you get 5,050.
A hexagon has exactly the same number of sides as it has angles: six.
Multiplying any number by 9 and adding up the digits of the answer always gives you 9 (try 9×7=63, and 6+3=9!).
The number 40, when written out as \"forty,\" is the only number spelled with letters in alphabetical order.
Ancient Egyptians used fractions over 4,000 years ago to divide bread and land fairly.
A \"palindrome number,\" like 121 or 3443, reads the same forwards and backwards.
The equal sign (=) was invented in 1557 by a mathematician who was tired of writing \"is equal to.\"
Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.
The number pi (π) never ends and never repeats — mathematicians have calculated trillions of its digits.
A \"baker\'s dozen\" means 13 instead of 12, an old tradition from bakers giving one extra item.
You can multiply by 5 quickly by multiplying by 10 and then dividing by 2.
The word \"hundred\" comes from an old word meaning \"a set of ten times ten.\"
A googolplex is 1 followed by a googol of zeros — a number too big to even write out!
Ancient Babylonians counted using a base-60 number system, which is why we have 60 minutes in an hour.
Any number multiplied by zero always equals zero — no matter how big the number is!
An abacus, one of the earliest calculating tools, is still used to teach math today.
A triangle\'s three angles always add up to exactly 180 degrees.
The Fibonacci sequence, found in sunflowers and seashells, starts 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13...
Zero was invented as a number relatively late in history, first used in ancient India.
Every even number greater than 2 can be split into two prime numbers added together.
The plus sign (+) comes from an old shorthand way of writing the Latin word \"et,\" meaning \"and.\"
A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.
Ancient Romans didn\'t have a symbol for zero at all in their numeral system.
A \"perfect number,\" like 6 or 28, equals the sum of all its smaller divisors (1+2+3=6!).
The multiplication sign (×) was first used in print in the year 1631.
Clocks are one of the few places we still count using both 12s and 60s instead of 10s.
A square number is what you get when you multiply a number by itself, like 4×4=16.
